steps.description:
You have a rack that can store up to 5 boxes. Below shows an example of what it looks with 2 boxes:

Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input the number of boxes (0-5). Use a list to store the information. 2. Call a function to display the rack following the example shown above.

You need to create a function that takes in the list to display.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - You may consider storing a rack list as follow (last item contains the number of boxes): [".", ".", ".", "=", "=", 2]

Test Input

0

3

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input boxes: 0

Example 2 Input boxes: 3

Your warehouse has a number of racks. Each rack can store up to 5 boxes. Below shows an example of what it looks like when you have 4 racks with some boxes.

Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input a list of integers from 0 to 5. The number of integers indicates the number of racks and each integer indicates the number of boxes in the respective rack. Generate the racks and use a 2D list to store the information. 2. Call a function to display the racks following the format shown above.

You need to create a function that takes in the 2D list to display.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - You may consider storing your 2D list as shown in the example below:

Test Input

1 3 2 3

1 0 2 5 3 3 4

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input boxes: 1 3 2 3

Example 2 Input boxes: 1 0 2 5 3 3 4

Your warehouse has a number of racks. Each rack can store up to 5 boxes. Below shows an example of what it looks like when you have 4 racks with some boxes.

Write a program that performs the following:

1. Ask user to input a list of integers from 0 to 5. The number of integers indicates the number of racks and each integer indicates the number of boxes in the respective rack. Generate the racks and use a 2D list to store the information. 2. Call a function to display the racks following the format shown above. 4. Call a function to find the rack with the least number of boxes and add one box to it. 5. Call a function to display the racks after adding the box. If there is more than one rack with minimum boxes, choose the leftmost rack.

Using the above example, a box will be added to the first rack. The final output will look as below.

Based on the above description, you need to create 2 functions: one to display and one to add the box. Think of what parameters to pass to your functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.
Hint:
- You may consider storing your 2D list as shown in the example below:
Test Input

1 3 2 3

2 3 1 5 1 3 4

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input boxes: 1 3 2 3

Example 2 Input boxes: 1 0 2 5 3 3 4

Your warehouse has a number of racks. Each rack can store up to 5 boxes. Below shows an example of what it looks like when you have 4 racks with some boxes. Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input a list of integers from 0 to 5. The number of integers indicates the number of racks and each integer indicates the number of boxes in the respective rack. Generate the racks and use a 2D list to store the information. 2. Call a function to display the racks following the format shown above. 3. Ask user to input the number of new boxes to be added. 4. Call a function to add the boxes one at a time, each time adding to the rack with the least number of boxes. If there is more than one rack with minimum boxes, choose the leftmost rack. 5. Call a function to display the racks after the boxes are added.

Using the above example, if 3 boxes are to be added, it will first add to the first rack as it has the minimum. The first rack and third rack will both have the minimum next. The first rack is chosen as it is the left most rack. The third box then added to the third rack since it has the minimum. The final output will look as below.

Based on the above description, you need to create 2 functions: one to display and one to add the boxes. Think of what parameters to pass to your functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment on your codes.
Test Input

1 3 2 3 4

1 0 2 5 3 3 4 10

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input box list: 1 3 2 3 Input boxes to add: 4

Example 2 Input box list: 1 0 2 5 3 3 4

Input boxes to add: 10
